title: git status
definition: Displays the state of the working directory and the staging area. It lets you see which changes have been staged, which haven't, and which files aren't being tracked by Git.
simpleExplanation: The most used command in Git. It's like asking Git: 'Hey, what's going on right now?' It tells you what branch you are on, and lists out exactly which files you have modified, added, or deleted.
realWorldExample: You come back to your computer after a lunch break. You forgot what files you were editing. You type `git status` to instantly see your unsaved progress.

basic: What color does `git status` usually use to show files that are in the Staging Area?
intermediate: What does it mean if a file is listed under 'Untracked files'?

answers.question: Color of staged files?
answers.answer: Green. Files that are modified but NOT staged are usually Red.

answers.question: Untracked files?
answers.answer: It means you created a brand new file, and Git has never seen it before. Git won't save it unless you explicitly tell it to by running `git add`.

codeExample:
$ git status
On branch main
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.

Changes to be committed:
  (use "git restore --staged <file>..." to unstage)
        modified:   index.html

Changes not staged for commit:
  (use "git add <file>..." to update what will be committed)
  (use "git restore <file>..." to discard changes in working directory)
        modified:   styles.css

Untracked files:
  (use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
        new-image.png
